issues.summary: Blueprint v2 'Skills bound' prose lossy-summarizes cc-design.md's detailed agent-frontmatter specifications; full canonical YAML frontmatter blocks not in Blueprint

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Provides explicit per-agent specs: Tools (with brackets), Skills (with brackets), Memory, Reasoning configuration (model/effort). All 5 new agents fully specified.

Provides prose-form 'Skills bound:' entries that summarize only the skill set (and even that lossily — see I-AA-302); no Tools list, no Memory directive, no YAML frontmatter block matching the canonical agent-file pattern.
Canonical pattern: name, description, model, effort, tools, skills, memory all declared. Blueprint should provide this content for new agents at integration-stage grade.

issues.impact: The Plan stage authors agent definition files. Without complete agent-frontmatter specifications in the Blueprint, the Plan author either (a) reads cc-design.md directly (defeating the Blueprint's role as integration substrate and risking Plan misinterpretation of per-layer details), or (b) invents the frontmatter from prose (introducing the 'improvised on each run' anti-pattern this feature is designed to eliminate). This is the precise failure mode FR-7 was authored to prevent — pipeline runs missing structured outputs because Blueprint was incomplete.
issues.recommended_resolution: Add an 'Agent Frontmatter Specifications' subsection to the Main Components section (or as a sibling subsection). Provide a literal YAML frontmatter block per new agent, transcribed from cc-design.md's specifications, in the canonical format. The five new agents each get a YAML block; the modified `shared-document-reviewer` doesn't need a new block (frontmatter unchanged; only body content updated).

issues.summary: Blueprint v2 'Skills bound' prose contradicts cc-design.md for every one of the 5 new agents

evidence.quote_paraphrase: Blueprint: 'auditing-shared (for log_state_transition.py, validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py access); KB-documentation-criteria'. cc-design: '[KB-cc-platform, KB-cc-design, recipe-feature-pipeline, auditing-shared, KB-review-disciplines]'. Blueprint omits KB-cc-platform, KB-cc-design, recipe-feature-pipeline, KB-review-disciplines.
Blueprint: 'ai-development-guide; plus task-domain-specific'. cc-design: '[ai-development-guide, KB-cc-design] plus task-spec-declared'. Blueprint omits KB-cc-design.
Blueprint: 'ai-development-guide; auditing-shared'. cc-design: '[ai-development-guide, KB-cc-design, auditing-shared]'. Blueprint omits KB-cc-design.
Blueprint: 'auditing-shared; KB-review-disciplines'. cc-design: '[KB-cc-design, KB-review-disciplines, auditing-shared]'. Blueprint omits KB-cc-design.

Blueprint: 'None directly bound; consumes phase-quality-report data structure'. cc-design: '[KB-cc-design, KB-review-disciplines, auditing-shared]'. Blueprint declares NONE; cc-design specifies three KBs.

issues.impact: Five direct contradictions between the integrated Blueprint and the approved per-layer design. The design-composer's role is integration + arbitration; if the composer departed from cc-design's specs, the departure needs an explicit rationale in the Blueprint. None is provided — the Blueprint v2 'Skills bound' prose appears to be a lossy summary rather than an intentional override. The execute-finalize-reconciler 'None directly bound' is the most consequential single contradiction because cc-design has it bound to 3 KBs and the agent class precedent (planning-side finalize-reconciler has 2 KBs) makes 'None' clearly wrong.
issues.recommended_resolution: Adopt cc-design.md's specifications verbatim in blueprint-v3 (the per-layer design has reviewer_verdict=approved and was the substrate the Blueprint should integrate, not override). Frame the v3 update as 'restore cc-design.md's agent specifications to the Blueprint' rather than 'new specifications.'

issues.summary: Blueprint v2 does not specify `tools:` field for any of the 5 new agents in agent-frontmatter form

evidence.quote_paraphrase: No agent has a Tools entry in agent-frontmatter list form (e.g., '[Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Bash(python3:*), TaskCreate, TaskUpdate]'). Tool invocations appear in narrative prose only.

Each of the 5 agents has explicit Tools list per cc-design: execute-orchestrator '[Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Task, TaskUpdate]'; code-producer '[Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash]'; quality-handler '[Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]'; phase-quality-reviewer '[Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write]'; execute-finalize-reconciler '[Read, Glob, Grep, Task, Write]'.
Every existing agent's `tools:` field is declared as a YAML list in the agent file frontmatter. The Blueprint specification at integration grade should provide this content.

issues.impact: Same as I-AA-301 — Plan-stage authoring is under-substrated. Plan author has to either read cc-design directly (substrate-passthrough antipattern) or invent.
issues.recommended_resolution: Include the cc-design Tools list in each agent's frontmatter spec in blueprint-v3.

issues.summary: Blueprint v2 does not specify `memory:` directive for any of the 5 new agents

evidence.quote_paraphrase: No Memory entry in any agent's specification.
Specifies: orchestrator 'memory: project'; code-producer 'memory: none'; quality-handler 'memory: none'; phase-quality-reviewer 'memory: none'; execute-finalize-reconciler 'memory: project'.
Every existing agent declares 'memory: project'. The value 'memory: none' is not used by any existing agent — its validity as a Claude Code platform directive is unverified.

issues.impact: Without `memory:` directive, the Plan author defaults to some implicit value (or omits the field). Also: cc-design's introduction of 'memory: none' is a divergence from existing convention that warrants explicit acknowledgment.
issues.recommended_resolution: Include `memory:` in each agent's frontmatter spec in blueprint-v3. Adopt cc-design's value choices but flag 'memory: none' as a new value requiring platform-validity verification in a Gate 4 open question (I-AA-308).

issues.impact: 'Edit' may be a valid Claude Code tool name for str_replace-style edits (distinct from full-file Write), but its absence from all existing agent declarations is conspicuous. The Plan author needs to know whether 'Edit' is platform-valid or whether 'Write' alone suffices.
issues.recommended_resolution: Include 'Edit' in blueprint-v3's code-producer frontmatter spec per cc-design, but flag for Gate 4 verification as part of I-AA-308 (platform-directive validity questions).

issues.summary: cc-design binds 'auditing-shared' as a Skill in 4 of 5 new agents; no existing agent binds 'auditing-shared' in `skills:`

evidence.section: all execute-* agents that invoke audit scripts
evidence.quote_paraphrase: Skills lists include 'auditing-shared' (e.g., quality-handler skills: '[ai-development-guide, KB-cc-design, auditing-shared]').

Zero existing agents declare 'auditing-shared' or any auditing-* skill in their `skills:` field. shared-document-reviewer invokes auditing-shared scripts via Bash but declares only KB-* skills in `skills:`.
'user-invocable: false; loaded by the audit-module skills via subprocess dispatch.' The skill self-describes as loaded by other SKILLS via subprocess dispatch, not by AGENTS via `skills:` binding.

Two readings: (a) cc-design is establishing a new convention (agents can bind auditing-shared in `skills:` to load its SKILL.md as context); (b) cc-design is conflating two surfaces (loaded-as-context vs invoked-via-Bash). Either is defensible if surfaced.

issues.impact: If reading (a) is correct, the new convention is fine and just needs explicit acknowledgment. If (b), the Blueprint should drop `auditing-shared` from `skills:` and rely on Bash invocation alone.
issues.recommended_resolution: Adopt cc-design's binding (reading a) in blueprint-v3 — `auditing-shared` listed in `skills:` for the 4 new agents that invoke its scripts. Add a brief note in the Agent Frontmatter Specifications subsection explaining the convention extension (this is the first project-side instance of a non-KB skill being bound; documents the precedent for future agents).
